_readme: Providers turned down by hand during review of discover_providers.cjs proposals. Read by verify, which skips these hosts. Every entry needs a reason: a blocklist without reasons becomes superstition, and the next person cannot tell a considered judgement from a typo. Removing an entry is fine once the site changes; that is what the date is for.

veterinariveteros.com.why: The only language sentence on the site is a customer review in the third person: 'The staff is highly skilled, speaks English and takes well care of the customers and their lovely furry friends'. That is somebody else's words about the clinic, which this directory does not accept from Google and should not accept here either. No pattern catches it safely: it carries no 'I' or 'my', and anything broad enough to match it also matches real sentences a clinic writes about its own staff.

en.smileandshine.co.th.why: Its only language sentence attributes the claim to somebody else: 'rated by GCR.com as one of the best English-speaking clinics'. That is a rating site's characterisation quoted on the clinic's page, not the clinic stating what it works in, and it is the same class of evidence as a review. If the clinic says it plainly somewhere else on its site, a later run will find that sentence instead and this entry should be removed.

jhouse.vn.why: Its only language sentence is a client testimonial naming the agent: "Ivy truly listens to what her clients are looking for and speaks excellent English, which is a huge plus!". A customer's words about a named employee, not the agency stating what it works in. The third-person review rule cannot see it, because the subject is a name rather than she, he or they. If the site says it plainly elsewhere, remove this entry.
